- URL: https://github.com/Hongchen030/mstATA
- Exact inspected revision: `4c6ec22caba582b3f3b6d82559a7fd52b4f6a3cf`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: mature R mixed-integer automated-test-assembly engine for single-stage forms and multistage-testing panels. It supports item-information/ICC-driven objectives, capped-maximin, maximin/minimax/weighted-sum and goal-programming objectives, enemy-item and stimulus constraints, exact/conditional stimulus selection, mixed-format pools, item-reuse limits, multiple panels, feasibility diagnostics and solver adapters for Gurobi, HiGHS, GLPK, lpSolve and SYMPHONY.
- Buyer/problem: certification/licensure bodies, assessment publishers and regulated workforce/compliance-training vendors spend expensive psychometrician/operations time assembling parallel forms and MST panels while maintaining blueprint/content, exposure and precision constraints; infeasible blueprints are often discovered late.
- Likely first paid wedge: fixed-price Assessment Blueprint Feasibility & Form Assembly Audit using a customer-owned item bank to prove feasibility/infeasibility, produce defensible parallel/MST forms, quantify information/classification tradeoffs and identify which constraints must relax when a blueprint cannot be satisfied.
- Monetization: fixed-fee blueprint/form audit -> managed form assembly -> recurring assessment-operations SaaS or embedded optimization service.
- Build-time/data advantage: roughly 2–4+ months of psychometrics/optimization engineering and domain-discovery compression; solver abstraction and diagnostic machinery are unusually complete for a zero-star repository.
- Evidence inspected: `R/solve_model.R`; `tests/testthat/test-solve_model.R`; recursive source/tests/vignettes tree. The solver test parametrizes seven MILP problems across five solvers and validates status, objective, solution and residuals. Source/vignettes cover bottom-up, top-down and hybrid MST, stimulus constraints, multi-objective formulations and infeasibility resolution.
- Actual public license / rights: MIT (`DESCRIPTION` says `MIT + file LICENSE`; repository `LICENSE.md` inspected). User's standing assertion of separate commercial permission also applies to repository-owned code/content. External solver terms such as Gurobi/FICO-style commercial products are not covered by that assertion; open solver paths exist. Bundled `.rda`/demo item pools require separate provenance review before commercial data reuse.
- Score: A4 / B5 / C5 / D5 / E5 / F5 = 29/30. The paid audit is fast but requires item-bank onboarding; enterprise ceiling, domain compression, rarity, evidence and repository-code rights are all excellent.
- Combination opportunities: strengthens the Assessment Evidence OS: MasteryTrace/Feng-Ji BKT provide longitudinal mastery evidence; `cdCAT`/`cat-irt-engine` handle adaptive administration; mstATA adds offline blueprint feasibility, parallel-form construction and MST panel governance.
- Next action: benchmark synthetic/customer-owned banks with deliberately feasible and infeasible blueprints; require exact constraint satisfaction, diagnostic explanation of infeasibility, solve-time stability and known precision/classification tradeoff recovery.

## 2026-09-19 — Merchant inventory recovery and promotion/pricing validation

### arunsah10/EventCart-Distributed-Inventory-Engine — WATCH — 22/30
- URL: https://github.com/arunsah10/EventCart-Distributed-Inventory-Engine
- Exact inspected revision: `3397a9e23f330c1d1ebb1e791020c2b814c09baf`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: distributed high-demand inventory/reservation stack using Spring Boot, Redis reservation state, Postgres/Flyway, Kafka, transactional outbox, idempotency, reservation expiry and a reconciliation scheduler that detects Redis reservation metadata with no corresponding DB reservation and republishes/retries before releasing stock. It also contains purchase/payment/order flows, rate limiting, DLQ monitoring and integration tests.
- Buyer/problem: merchants/ticketing/high-demand commerce operators lose revenue and trust to oversells, abandoned holds, duplicate purchase events and Redis/DB/Kafka divergence during spikes and failures.
- Likely first paid wedge: fixed-price Flash-Sale / Inventory Reservation Failure Audit that injects duplicate checkouts, delayed/duplicated Kafka events, expired holds and Redis/Postgres divergence and quantifies oversell/cancelled-order risk.
- Monetization: reliability audit -> implementation hardening -> recurring high-demand-launch assurance/merchant-ops monitoring.
- Build-time/data advantage: roughly 1–2+ months of distributed reservation/outbox/reconciliation workflow discovery.
- Evidence inspected: recursive tree with substantive authentication, purchase, inventory, reservation-expiry, outbox and Redis tests; `ReservationReconciliationScheduler.java`; `FlashSaleConcurrencyIntegrationTest.java`. The reconciliation scheduler has real orphan detection/retry/release logic. Important evidence caveat: the inspected flash-sale concurrency test runs a real Spring context but mocks core Redis services and asserts only that some requests are allowed/rejected, so it does not yet prove a hard no-oversell invariant under real Redis contention.
- Actual public license / rights: no root `LICENSE` found at the exact revision; user's standing separate commercial permission is assumed for repository-owned code/content. Redis/Kafka/Postgres/other external dependencies retain their own terms.
- Score: A4 / B4 / C4 / D3 / E3 / F4 = 22/30. Fast measurable reliability wedge and real recovery workflow; rarity/evidence are below the MASTER leaders because concurrency proof is weak and the reconciliation scan is not yet production-scale.
- Combination opportunities: strengthens the merchant-operations/warehouse cluster with `kayc529/tender-chops-ecommerce`: reserve -> authorize/revalidate -> outbox/event delivery -> expiry/reconciliation -> final inventory outcome.
- Non-sensitive exposure metadata: repository root contains a committed `.env` path at this revision. Contents were deliberately NOT opened, copied, preserved or tested. Status is unknown. Remediation note only: replace committed secret-bearing env files with `.env.example`/secret-manager references and rotate any real credentials if the owner determines they were ever present.
- Next action: run a real Redis+Postgres 100–1000-concurrent-checkout benchmark with duplicate/reordered events, Redis restart and Kafka redelivery; require no oversell, exact reservation release and reconciliation convergence.
